# Learning Goals: One Effective Exam Prep Strategy

**Generated by:** Skill 02 — Learning Goals
**Workshop slug:** exam_prep_strategy
**Bloom's level:** Apply
**ARIVA format:** 10-minute workshop

---

## Intended Learning Outcome (ILO)

By the end of this workshop, participants will be able to:

> **Use** retrieval practice as a study method by recalling course content from memory without looking at notes, and identifying gaps to guide further study.

---

## Why This ILO

"Apply" is the right Bloom's level here because the workshop does not just ask students to name or describe the strategy — it asks them to actually do it during the Verarbeitung phase. The ILO is achievable in 10 minutes because retrieval practice has a zero-setup, instantly executable form: close your notes and write down what you remember. The 10-minute format cannot deliver mastery of spaced scheduling, habit formation, or a full study overhaul — but it can deliver one completed retrieval attempt and the cognitive shift that comes with it.

---

## How the ILO Maps to ARIVA

| Phase | What it does for the ILO |
|---|---|
| **A — Arrival** | Announces the ILO directly: "you'll be able to use retrieval practice to study for your exams" |
| **R — Reactivating** | Surfaces the problem the ILO solves — the gap between effort and exam performance |
| **I — Informing** | Explains what retrieval practice is and why it works better than re-reading |
| **V — Verarbeitung** | Participants do one complete retrieval practice attempt with their own material |
| **A — Assessing** | Checks whether participants identified at least one gap — the signal that the method worked |

---

## Assessing Question

The ILO is checked in the final 60 seconds with this question:

> "Hands up — who just discovered at least one thing they thought they knew but couldn't actually recall?"

A participant has met the ILO if: they attempted recall and can identify at least one gap in their knowledge — demonstrating that they have used the strategy, not merely understood it.

---

## What This Workshop Does NOT Cover

To protect the 10-minute scope, the following are explicitly out of scope:

- **Spaced repetition** — the complementary scheduling strategy that maximises retrieval practice over time; requires its own session
- **Other high-utility learning strategies** (elaborative interrogation, practice testing with feedback, interleaving) — this session goes deep on one, not wide across several
- **How to build a full exam study plan** — the session delivers the core mechanism, not a time-management system

---

## Facilitator Note

State the ILO in the Arrival phase as a concrete action: "By the end of this, you'll have already used the most effective study technique most students never use — and you'll know exactly why it works." This primes participants to expect to *do* something, not just listen.
